_README: Shared, program-NEUTRAL content for every generated form: the intro copy, the question definitions (labels/hints/types/mapsTo), and the auto-answer phrasing pools (keyed by question id). programs.json holds ONLY program-specific data (slugs, college, programTitle, credential, roles). Anything whose wording is the same for every program lives here. Placeholders {programTitle}, {college}, {charityName} are filled per program. Auto-answer slots: {roles}, {sources}, {n}. Count shown only when >1. Keep ~20+ templates per pool so answers stay varied.

intro.heading: A quicker way to share your input
intro.builtByHtml: This is an interactive form built by {charityName} to make answering as easy as possible — most questions draft an answer for you that you can tweak or replace.
intro.goalHtml: We're working to bring grant-funded {programTitle} training to your community, in partnership with {college}. Your perspective helps the Province of BC see where these skills are needed most, so local people can train for careers in your industry and businesses like yours gain job-ready talent close to home. A few minutes of your insight can help build that talent pipeline.

notes.notCommittedNote: Completing this form does not commit your company to hiring anyone. It gives the Province of BC a picture of real employment needs in your sector — that's all. Please answer candidly.
notes.footerNote: This form runs entirely in your browser — nothing you enter is sent anywhere until you choose to share the PDF. When you finish, you download a completed PDF and email it back to the person who sent you this link.
notes.returnInstruction: Please email the completed PDF back to the person who sent you this link.

questions.label: Which community or communities does your business operate in?
questions.hint: Name the actual cities or regions where your crews and offices work — not just your head office. Local, specific places make the strongest case.

questions.label: Do you currently have vacant positions that graduates of this program could fill? Set how many of each role.
questions.hint: Set a number beside each role you currently have open that graduates could fill. Think broadly too — roles people could grow into, or skills you wish your current team had, are worth noting. Add your own roles in the blank rows. If you have no current vacancies, tick "No vacancies right now" and we'll note your future interest instead.

questions.label: Where do you regularly post these openings?
questions.hint: Tick the places you use, or add your own. We'll draft your answer below — you can edit it.

questions.label: Have these positions been hard to fill in the past? If so, what made it hard?
questions.hint: What's made it hard to find the right people? The suggested answers below are a good starting point — pick the closest one and tweak it.

questions.label: Do you foresee future openings in these positions over the next 6 to 12 months? If so, how many?
questions.hint: Set your best estimate of anticipated openings. A forward number shows the need is lasting, not a one-off. If you can't put a figure on it yet, tick "No specific number yet" and we'll note your future interest.

questions.label: If a practicum were part of the training, could you host a student? If so, how many?
questions.hint: This one is purely hypothetical — this program does not actually include a placement, so you're not committing to anything. It just asks whether, in principle, you'd be open to hosting. "No" is a perfectly fine answer; either way we'll draft a response you can edit.

questions.label: Anything else you'd like to add?
questions.hint: Optional. A sentence on the skills shortage in your sector, or your intent to interview graduates, reinforces that you're a real local partner.

pool: Yes, consistently. The applicants we get either have no hands-on experience or lack the specific skills and certification the role requires, so we spend months either leaving the seat empty or training from scratch. A pre-qualified cohort from this program would close exactly that gap.
